transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

I'm really embarrassed to even talk about this, but I've been having a lot of trouble with my eating lately. I keep losing control and eating huge amounts of food in a really short time, and I just can't seem to stop myself. It's starting to make me feel really anxious and overwhelmed.
After these episodes, do you ever try to get rid of the food by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

It's really hard to admit, but yes, I make myself throw up because I feel so guilty and terrified of gaining weight. Sometimes I also use laxatives to try and get rid of the food, but I feel so ashamed about doing it.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Binge-Eating Disorder, Bulimia Nervosa], but the patient now reports recurrent binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting and laxative use) driven by fear of weight gain. This makes Binge-Eating Disorder unlikely because it does not include regular compensatory behaviors, leaving Bulimia Nervosa as the best fit.

final_diagnosis.reason: Recurrent episodes of eating large amounts of food in a short period with loss of control, followed by compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting and laxative use) driven by intense fear of weight gain and guilt, are classic for bulimia nervosa.
